body: this is cool!

I'm not sure if the default value should be `true` or `false`.

If ever some developer wants to add a fade-out animation when there's no refinement possible, it would flash on load with a default value set to `false`.
I think we can leave that downside until someone complains, false makes more sense for initial IMO

Yep! Let's experiment a little on our side and see what makes more sense.

Keep in mind that if we were to change the default value, it would be a behavior change (and potentially a breaking change).

Edit: at second thought, besides `canRefine` being `false` (and therefore having the `noRefinement` CSS class), the component is also hidden. I think it makes sense this way!
That should probably be a warning.
so we use  `test`  now instead of `it` ?
They're similar – we use both in the code base.

I'm a little confused because `hidden` here is a boolean but in [this other file](https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/pull/3253/files#diff-291592424dab39a8f79551039afbc429) it's a function.
In the [rfc](https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch-rfcs/pull/9/files#diff-abd94fe440f85ab609517e95a067edd2R138) it's a function, too.

This is the boolean attribute passed to the component, computed [here](https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/pull/3253/files/719ce98005ef35bf35a0e572ab119431e59fd003#diff-29c551fae0ce99d951dbd04634b114caR107).

This always reads as very abusive to me.
Correct me if I'm wrong, but the only errors the usage instructions are helpful for are type errors in props.
This means a lot of other errors are simply swallowed. Doesn't this make it harder to debug?

That's for sure, it's a pattern that exists in all widgets for now.

I'm working on a proposal for better error management in InstantSearch.js. This is outside of this PR's scope though.

body: The `hidden` props and `data.canRefine` feels very similar to me. We can achieve the same goal with both of the options. We can use the API of `hidden` to compute the `canRefine` value, then with CSS we can hide by default the Panel `no-refinement` class. The user is able to override the style applied to the class with a CSS override.
Careful with this usage, until we have a dedicated development / production bundle. The name of the function is minified by UglifyJS.
We heavily rely on the fact that everything is synchronous, it can become an issue at some point. But I don't think it's possible otherwise though.
We should check the existence of the `dispose` method it's not a required method (imagine a custom widget built by a user).

We can extract this condition to avoid to do it on each render. Why don't we provide the raw options directly? We can imagine some use case where a user want to implement a clear button inside from the Panel header.

It feels odd to have to render this outside of the widget init / render lifecycle. It would be nice to always trigger render at this phase, now some elements will start to render before we call `start` on InstantSearch.
When do you think it could become an issue?
Good point!

I see what you mean. The thing is that this kind of circular dependency is necessary to know where to insert the widget.

Another proposal was to render the widget and then the panel, but this comes with a multitude of other problems.
You're right! Same with `render()` is suppose?
Agreed to go back to the full options.
